evidence.senderRole: the pool paying the token out to a buyer
evidence.recipientRole: the counterparty of the taxed transfer
evidence.poolRole: a constant-product pool holding this token, used here to show that pool-side transfers are taxed
evidence.requestedAmountDerivation: the transfer is internal to a swap, so amount is reconstructed as transferToRecipient + transferToTaxDestination; the exact floor identity below confirms the reconstruction.
evidence.computation: One transfer of 5542177559656802884719 emits two Transfer events with the same sender: 5486755784060234855871 to 0xc2d0d7b1d50b07a14a4b0edcb39af283cd9e9781 and 55421775596568028848 to 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000. transferToRecipient = floor(amount * 99000 / 100000); fee = amount - transferToRecipient reproduces BOTH emitted amounts EXACTLY, so the measured tax is 184739251988560096160000/1847392519885600961573 bps == 100 bps up to the one-base-unit floor residue.
evidence.corroboration: the same floor identity at 100 bps holds on 51 independent two-leg transfers of this token found by replaying eth_getLogs, 13 of which have the pool 0xbecdd069e7325eb04ea77bab78d16d0f5e8c7e0c as an endpoint (1 pool->user, 12 user->pool).
evidence.reproduce: eth_getLogs on address 0xe1fb1bc7a6d1b067defe7f9ce01ab4b5c931803f at block 45138174 for topic0 0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef, then group by (transactionHash, topics[1]) and look for the two legs sharing this sender.

note: Fee-on-transfer token: a taxed transfer emits TWO Transfer events with the SAME sender -- 99% of the amount to the intended recipient and 1% burned to the zero address. Both legs are in the receipt, so the split is reproducible from eth_getLogs alone with no tracing. The fee is a floored integer division, so the realised rate equals 100 bps up to a rounding residue of at most one base unit; the exact rational for the cited transaction is in evidence.taxBpsExactRational. Confirmed on 51 independent two-leg transfers, 13 of them with the pool 0xbecdd069e7325eb04ea77bab78d16d0f5e8c7e0c as an endpoint, so pool-side transfers ARE taxed -- which is what makes the token unsafe as a routing hop rather than merely unusual. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE -- the destination pool receives only 99% of amountSent, so pool.swap(amount0Out, ...) reverts K() because the demanded output assumed the full amountSent; (2) as TERMINAL OUTPUT -- no next pool and no K() revert, but the user receives 99% of the quoted amountOut, silently violating the minAmountOut slippage promise (delivered < quoted). Both modes are unsafe.
